ui.hero: Business applications and automation for growing companies
ui.intro: I help small and medium-sized businesses simplify everyday work, connect their existing systems and reduce manual data entry. I build business applications, integrations and practical AI tools around the way your company works.
ui.contactText: Tell me how your company works today and what you would like to improve. You do not need a technical specification. We can work out whether to connect existing tools, automate a task or build an application. Scope, pricing and maintenance arrangements are agreed before work starts.
ui.bioText: I have been programming since 2018. My experience includes PHP and Laravel web applications, React development and machine learning projects. I have worked on projects at Matysart and taught programming at Coding Giants. Teaching AI, Python and other technologies helps me explain technical choices clearly.
steps: Understand your workflow — you describe the process, the difficulties and the tools you use.
Choose an approach — we consider existing tools and agree scope, pricing and how to evaluate the result.
First version — I build a selected part of the application or a prototype, and we gather feedback from users.
Launch and next steps — we put the solution into use, cover day-to-day operation and agree maintenance arrangements.

services.title: Business applications and system integrations
services.intro: For B2B trading, distribution and service companies where handling orders, managing jobs or transferring data involves too much manual work. We can extend an existing application, connect your tools or build a system around the workflow.

details.heading: Software built around everyday work
paragraphs: A custom system makes sense when a recurring workflow matters to the business and existing products do not handle it well enough.
items: Internal tools for employees to manage jobs, requests and orders.
Customer and partner portals with access to their own information.
Extending existing applications instead of replacing the entire system.

details.heading: Workflow automation and system integrations
paragraphs: When your applications already do their jobs well, connecting them may be the right approach. We first identify where data comes from, where it needs to go and who is responsible for its accuracy.
items: Data exchange through available application programming interfaces (APIs).
Automating selected sales and internal operations.
Generating reports from agreed data sources.
Error handling, operation logs and agreed access permissions.

details.heading: When to build and when to use an existing product
paragraphs: If an off-the-shelf product can support your workflow with configuration, there is no need to build a copy. Custom software is worth considering for specific workflows, connected data or limitations in an existing system.

Before estimating the work, we check system access, documentation, integration constraints and ongoing maintenance costs. Some tools do not expose data in a way that makes integration straightforward.

details.heading: Where to start
paragraphs: Choose one workflow, such as transferring orders or preparing a report. Describe how it works today and which tools you use. We can agree where to start and how to assess the results.

services.title: Practical AI implementations
services.intro: For businesses where employees search across many documents or repeatedly process similar text. We first check whether AI is needed and whether the available data can support a useful solution.

details.heading: Where AI can help
items: An assistant answering questions from company documents.
Internal knowledge search with links to sources.
Classifying requests and organising text information.
Draft summaries and content for an employee to review.
Connecting a language model to an existing application.

details.heading: Answer quality and limitations
paragraphs: We start with representative questions or tasks and agree evaluation criteria. We test accuracy, source references and what happens when information is missing. Important decisions and content need appropriate human review.

Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) finds relevant company material and supplies it to a model as context. This helps ground answers in documents but does not eliminate errors. A conventional search tool may be a better choice for simple retrieval.

details.heading: Data, permissions and running costs
paragraphs: Before a prototype, we agree which data may be processed, who may access it and whether it can be sent to an external model provider. User permissions must also apply to retrieval and generated answers.
Storage, provider terms, operation logs and error handling depend on the implementation. We discuss model usage, hosting and maintenance costs separately.

details.heading: Start with a small prototype
paragraphs: We choose one task and an agreed dataset. A prototype tests quality and costs before a broader integration. If it falls short of the criteria, we adjust the approach or leave AI out of that workflow.

audience.heading: Who I work with
audience.intro: I primarily work with small and medium-sized B2B trading, distribution and service businesses.

cards.heading: Trade and distribution
cards.text: Order handling, partner portals and information flowing between sales and back-office tools.

cards.heading: B2B services
cards.text: Jobs and service requests, employee tools, customer portals and reporting.

cards.heading: Scattered company knowledge
cards.text: Documents and information spread across applications that employees need to access more easily.

problems.heading: Does this sound like your business?

cards.heading: Your team enters the same data more than once
cards.text: People move information between spreadsheets, email and business tools.
cards.solution: Connect existing systems and automate data transfers.
cards.benefit: Less manual data entry and a lower risk of mistakes.

cards.heading: Orders and customer requests are hard to track
cards.text: Updates on ongoing jobs get lost in email, and customers keep asking for the same information.
cards.solution: A shared job-management panel or customer portal.
cards.benefit: Clearer status updates and easier access to the information people need.

cards.heading: Finding an answer means searching several places
cards.text: Instructions, decisions and documentation are scattered.
cards.solution: An organised knowledge base, search tool or AI assistant with source references.
cards.benefit: Easier information retrieval while respecting access permissions.

cards.heading: Direct collaboration
cards.text: You work directly with me, from understanding the problem through to delivery. We agree priorities and scope together.

cards.heading: Technology that fits the need
cards.text: I start by looking at your current tools. An integration or a configured off-the-shelf product may be enough.

cards.heading: A manageable first step
cards.text: We can start with one workflow or a prototype. We plan further development around your business needs and feedback from users.

cards.heading: Applications and AI together
cards.text: I combine application development with machine learning, proposing AI where its usefulness and quality can be evaluated.

offerings.heading: Custom business applications
offerings.text: Order and job management, employee tools and customer portals, when off-the-shelf software does not fit your workflow.

offerings.heading: Workflow automation and integrations
offerings.text: Connect sales and internal tools, transfer data and generate reports. A focused starting point for improving one repetitive process.

offerings.heading: Practical AI implementations
offerings.text: Search company documents, build assistants that answer questions using those documents and process text, with quality checks, access controls and model limitations in mind.
